newsitem.title: USA: GM sees OnStar system in more 1998 models.
newsitem.headline: GM sees OnStar system in more 1998 models.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday it hopes to expand its OnStar navigation and security systems into other lines than its Cadillac luxury car division by the 1998 model year.

"The plan right now would have us in almost one vehicle line in every market division next year," Chet Huber, general manager of GM's OnStar unit, told reporters following a presentation at the North American International Auto Show.
GM also will be working over the next two years to spread the technology into more models, he said.
The optional system, which utilizes global positioning system satellite technolgy, has a suggested retail price of $895, plus installation, and a $22.50 monthly fee.
The system is being expanded through partnerships with other companies to provide more directional data, such as information on the nearest gas station, Huber told reporters.
Future applications could include allowing a customer to have a service station provide a diagnosis on a problem without the driver bringing the car to the station, he said.
So far, about 10 percent of buyers have chosen OnStar when it is an available option, Huber said.
The system will also be featured in an advertising campaign this year, with a Mercedes, a Lexus and a Cadillac (with OnStar) all shown trying to navigate a maze.
